groups.label: Global / Engine
groups.info: Core render settings for the whole material: culling, stencil masking, proximity fade, and ColorChord. Most avatars can leave these at default.

groups.label: Stencil & Sorting
groups.info: Stencil masking, used to hide the body under clothing or order overlapping transparent parts. Leave at default unless you are setting up a clothing mask.

groups.label: Advanced Render State
groups.info: Raw render state. These are power-user overrides - wrong values can make the material invisible or z-fight. Leave at defaults unless you know why you are changing them.

groups.label: Camera Proximity Fade
groups.info: Fades the avatar out as the viewer's camera gets close, so you do not block their view. Tune the near and far distances.

groups.label: AudioLink Response
groups.info: Smooths how every AudioLink effect reacts: a fast punch on the beat with a tunable tail, so reactions feel musical instead of twitchy. Affects break, glitch, speaker, emission, rim, and the rest.

groups.label: AudioLink ColorChord
groups.info: Drives emission colour from AudioLink ColorChord, so your glow shifts hue with the music's notes instead of a fixed colour.

groups.label: AudioLink Vertex FX
groups.info: Moves, rotates, and scales geometry with the music. Translation and scale lerp between Min and Max by band intensity. Speed and Accumulate modes use AudioLink Chronotensity, so motion glides and never snaps back when the music changes. Mask where it applies. Shadows and the standard outline follow the motion.

groups.label: Base & Color
groups.info: Your albedo texture, normal map, and colour tweaks (saturation, brightness, gamma, hue). The base look before lighting and effects.

groups.label: Decals
groups.info: Up to four image decals layered over the base colour, for tattoos, logos, or markings. Each has its own placement, blend, tint, and optional glow. Use textures with transparent edges so they sit cleanly.

groups.label: UV Tile Discard
groups.info: Hides mesh parts by their UV tile in a 4x4 grid: UV outfit pieces into separate tiles, then toggle each with a single animated float - no extra materials or bones. Vertex-level, so hidden parts cost nothing and cast no shadows. Each mesh island must sit fully inside one tile; a triangle spanning two tiles disappears with the discarded one. Tile (0,0) is the standard 0-1 UV square.

groups.label: Detail Maps
groups.info: High-tiling micro detail layered over the base: a detail albedo (grey = no change) and a detail normal for skin pores, fabric weave, or brushed metal that holds up at conversational distance. Masked, so skin detail stays off clothes. Pairs well with Subsurface Scattering.

groups.label: Lighting & Shadows
groups.info: How the surface reacts to light: toon or realistic shading, shadow strength, and ambient fill.

groups.label: Subsurface Scattering
groups.info: Soft under-skin light in two parts: a warm tinted band where light rolls into shadow, and light bleeding through thin areas like ears and fingers when lit from behind. Works with both lighting models. Mask it to skin only for the most realistic result.

groups.label: Reflections & Specular
groups.info: Metallic reflections, smoothness, anisotropic highlights, and clear coat. Reads the packed PBR map (R metallic, G AO, B smoothness).

groups.label: Anisotropic Highlights
groups.info: Stretched specular highlights that follow the surface grain, the look you get on brushed metal, hair, or silk.

groups.label: Stylized Specular (Toon)
groups.info: Anime style stepped specular highlights that stack on top of the normal specular. Each layer is one sharp highlight: Size sets how big it is, Feather how soft the edge, Strength how bright. Turn the base specular down if you want only this look.

groups.label: 2nd Specular / Clear Coat
groups.info: A second, sharper specular layer over the base, for a wet or lacquered clear coat shine.

groups.label: MatCaps
groups.info: Up to five fake lighting overlays from a sphere image. Great for metal, glass, or stylised rims without real lights.

groups.label: MatCap 0
groups.info: A MatCap fakes lighting from a sphere image. Pick a matcap texture, choose how it blends, and mask where it shows. Great for metal, glass, or rim light with no real lights.

groups.label: MatCap 1
groups.info: Another MatCap layer that stacks on top of the others. Same controls as MatCap Base.

groups.label: MatCap 2
groups.info: Another MatCap layer that stacks on top of the others. Same controls as MatCap Base.

groups.label: MatCap 3
groups.info: Another MatCap layer that stacks on top of the others. Same controls as MatCap Base.

groups.label: MatCap 4
groups.info: Another MatCap layer that stacks on top of the others. Same controls as MatCap Base.

groups.label: Emission
groups.info: Up to four independent glow layers, each maskable and AudioLink reactive. Most neon and glow lives here.

groups.label: Emission 0
groups.info: One emission layer: a mask, HDR colour and intensity, hue shift, and an audio mode. The bars below add AudioLink reactivity, light based dimming, blinking, and an infinity mirror.

groups.label: AudioLink Settings
groups.info: Makes this emission layer react to AudioLink. Pick a frequency band from bass to treble and how much it boosts brightness, plus optional extra bands and volume response.

groups.label: Light Based
groups.info: Dims or brightens this emission based on how lit the surface is, so the glow can fade in shadow or only show in the dark. Set the lighting range and the min and max multipliers.

groups.label: Blinking
groups.info: Pulses this emission on and off over time. Set the speed and how dim it goes at the bottom of each blink.

groups.label: Scan / Sweep
groups.info: A bright band that sweeps across this emission, vertically or horizontally, like a scanner. The same band travels, it does not reveal a bigger pattern underneath. Add Pixelation and Glitch Flicker for a chunky 32-bit look. Outside-Band Glow sets how much the rest of the mask still glows.

groups.label: Infinity Mirror
groups.info: Creates a recursive tunnel of repeating layers behind the surface, like an infinity mirror, using a background texture and parallax depth.

groups.label: Emission 1
groups.info: Another independent emission layer with the same controls as Emission 0. Stacks with the others.

groups.label: Emission 2
groups.info: Another independent emission layer with the same controls as Emission 0. Stacks with the others.

groups.label: Emission 3
groups.info: Another independent emission layer with the same controls as Emission 0. Stacks with the others.

groups.label: Special FX
groups.info: Optional stylised and reactive effects. Each is off by default and toggled on its own bar below.

groups.label: Audio Reactive
groups.info: Effects that pulse, ripple, and react to music through AudioLink.

groups.label: Stylized
groups.info: Looks and finishes: cosmic, retro, glass, glow, and other visual styles.

groups.label: Geometry
groups.info: Effects that reshape or break apart the mesh itself.

groups.label: Visibility & World
groups.info: Where, and to whom, the material appears.

groups.label: Interior Mapping (3D Room)
groups.info: Shows a believable 3D room behind the surface, like a window into an impossible space. Uses a room cubemap with real perspective, so it shifts correctly as you move around it. Great for chest panels, eyes, or portals.

groups.label: Window Variety
groups.info: Makes each window show a different room. Without this every window shows an identical interior, which is the main giveaway that interior mapping is a trick.

groups.label: Furniture Layer
groups.info: An optional cut-out layer suspended inside the room at its own distance. Because it sits between the window and the back wall, it shifts against the background as you move, which is what makes the interior feel like real space.

groups.label: Room Lights
groups.info: Lights the windows independently, switching over time and flickering, so a facade reads as occupied rather than uniformly lit.

groups.label: Glass and Edge
groups.info: How the glass in front of the interior distorts the view. Static Imperfection is fixed in the pane like real window glass; Ripple animates for water and aquarium looks.

groups.label: Refraction (Glass / Heat Haze)
groups.info: Bends whatever is rendered behind the surface, for glass, cloaks, or energy fields, with an optional chromatic split. It uses a GrabPass that is automatically stripped when this section is locked off, so it costs nothing unless you use it. Do not mark Enable Refraction as animated, or the strip cannot happen and the cost stays.

groups.label: Physical Glass
groups.info: Refraction derived from Snell's law rather than a screen offset. The view ray genuinely bends by the index of refraction, each colour bends by a slightly different amount so edges split into a prism fringe, and rough glass scatters what shows through.

groups.label: Screen Display (Live Audio)
groups.info: Turns a masked area into a live screen driven by the actual audio: an oscilloscope of the real waveform, or EQ bars per frequency band. Optional grid, LCD subpixels, scanlines, and a crash screen. Needs AudioLink for the live signal.

groups.label: Fresnel Rim (Edge Glow)
groups.info: A glow around the silhouette edges facing away from the camera, for a neon or holographic look.

groups.label: Speaker Ripple
groups.info: AudioLink driven ripples that pulse across the surface like a speaker cone reacting to bass.

groups.label: EQ Visualizer
groups.info: Maps AudioLink frequency bands onto the surface as a moving equaliser pattern.

groups.label: Iridescence
groups.info: A view dependent colour shift (oil slick / soap bubble) layered over the surface.

groups.label: Thin Film
groups.info: Physically based iridescence: the colours come from light interfering with itself inside a microscopically thin film, the same effect as a soap bubble or an oil slick. Hue shifts with viewing angle and film thickness rather than cycling through chosen colours.

groups.label: AudioLink Settings
groups.info: Makes the iridescence react to AudioLink. In Thin Film the beat physically shifts the film thickness, so the interference colours move; in Gradient it drives the phase. Pick a band, plus optional extra bands and volume response.

groups.label: Dissolve
groups.info: Burns the mesh away along a noise edge with a glowing burn line. Good for spawn in and despawn moments.

groups.label: Glitch Outline
groups.info: A stylised, flickering outline that jitters and breaks up, reactive to AudioLink.

groups.label: Outline (Inverted Hull)
groups.info: The classic toon / anime outline: a back-facing shell extruded around the mesh in a flat colour. Pick a colour and width, mask where it shows, optionally tint it by the texture or let it react to light. World width is a fixed thickness in metres (thins with distance); Screen width stays a constant on-screen thickness at any distance.

groups.label: Constellation / Nebula
groups.info: A starfield and nebula. Leave the Constellation Mask empty to cover the whole material, or assign one (white shows, black hides) to confine it to specific areas, like a window into space.

groups.label: AudioLink Settings
groups.info: Makes the starfield react to AudioLink. Pick a frequency band from bass to treble and how much it pops the stars, lines, and nebula, plus optional extra bands and volume response. Turn this off for a completely still, non-reactive starfield.

groups.label: Constellation Lines
groups.info: Draws faint lines linking nearby stars across the parallax layers. Because the layers drift at different speeds, links stretch, dim, and reconnect on their own as stars move apart and back together.

groups.label: Hologram
groups.info: Makes the avatar look like a projected hologram: object-space scanlines, rim glow, a sweep bar, flicker, glitch, and a see-through look. For the True Alpha style, set the material's Transparency Mode to a transparent option; the Dither style works in any mode.

groups.label: Plasma Hits
groups.info: Audio-reactive sci-fi hits that pop at random spots in the avatar's own 3D space and ripple outward, bumping the surface as they pass. Hits keep landing in new places and react to the audio bands (bass, low mids, high mids, treble). Stays dark below the Audio Threshold and when no AudioLink is present.

groups.label: Retro / PS1
groups.info: Emulates the PlayStation 1 look: wobbly vertex snapping, chunky texture pixelation, colour posterisation with ordered dithering, and CRT scanlines. Applied at the very end, so it flattens the whole material including the other effects, which is how a real PS1 rendered. Aesthetically the opposite of the rest of the shader, but a fun combo.

groups.label: UV Morph
groups.info: Warps the texture coordinates before anything samples them, so the whole surface swims, swirls, or glitches. Because it happens first, albedo, normals, emission and every other UV0 map distort together.

groups.label: AudioLink Settings
groups.info: Makes the distortion react to AudioLink. Pick a frequency band from bass to treble and how much it deepens and quickens the warp, plus optional extra bands and volume response.

groups.label: View Visibility
groups.info: Controls where this material shows up: in normal view (what you and other players see directly), in mirrors, and in cameras or photos, each independently. Turn a view off to hide the material there. For example, off in Normal but on in Mirror and Camera makes the material appear only in reflections and photos. Uses VRChat's mirror and camera globals, so it only takes effect in VRChat.

groups.label: Nebula
groups.info: A volumetric nebula that adds real depth inside the constellation areas. PC only and noticeably heavier.

groups.label: Geometry Break
groups.info: Shatters or floats the mesh into pieces, driven by an audio beat or a slow drift, with glow and fade options.

groups.label: Glitter / Sparkle
groups.info: Procedural sparkle flakes scattered over the surface that twinkle and glint as you move. Tune density, size, viewable angle, and speed, mask where they show, and optionally react to AudioLink or be lit by the world.

groups.label: Mesh Glitch
groups.info: Randomly displaces chunks of the mesh for a datamosh or digital glitch effect.

groups.label: Height & Parallax
groups.info: Adds fake surface depth from a height map, so detail appears to sit below the surface as you move.

groups.label: LTCGI
groups.info: Enables LTCGI area light support, so the avatar picks up coloured light from LTCGI world screens and emitters.

groups.label: VRC Light Volumes
groups.info: Support for VRC Light Volumes, the voxel-based light probe replacement modern worlds use. The avatar picks up per-pixel baked lighting and moving point, spot, and area Light Volume lights - far more detailed than Unity's blended probes. Falls back to normal probes automatically in worlds without it. Requires the free VRC Light Volumes package (red.sim.lightvolumes), version 2.1.3 or newer - installed automatically alongside the shader via VCC.

groups.label: Debug Views
groups.info: Renders one isolated term instead of the finished surface - albedo, normals, AO, ambient, and so on. Use it to find which input is wrong when a material looks black or blown out, rather than guessing from the composited result. Set it back to Off before locking: it drives an //ifex, so Off strips the whole feature from the locked shader, and anything else ships the debug view to everyone who sees you.

groups.label: VRSL GI
groups.info: Lighting from VRSL GI stage rigs - the moving heads, pars and spots in club and event worlds actually illuminate the avatar, with cone shapes respected. No package to install: the world publishes the light data as a global, so this simply switches itself on in worlds running VRSL GI and costs nothing everywhere else. It cannot be previewed in the editor, only in-world.

tooltips.name: _CullMode
tooltips.text: Which faces to draw. Back is normal and cheapest. Off draws both sides for flat cards or fins.

tooltips.name: _StencilRef
tooltips.text: The value this material writes or compares against. Keep it low, 1 to 3.

tooltips.name: _StencilComp
tooltips.text: How the stencil test passes. Always means no masking. NotEqual is the usual reader setting.

tooltips.name: _StencilPass
tooltips.text: What to write when the test passes. Replace stamps the reference (writer). Keep writes nothing.

tooltips.name: _StencilFail
tooltips.text: What to write when the stencil test fails. Usually Keep.

tooltips.name: _StencilZFail
tooltips.text: What to write when the depth test fails. Usually Keep.

tooltips.name: _StencilReadMask
tooltips.text: Bits considered when comparing. Leave at 255 unless layering multiple masks.

tooltips.name: _StencilWriteMask
tooltips.text: Bits allowed to be written. Leave at 255 unless layering multiple masks.

tooltips.name: _ZTest
tooltips.text: How the material tests against the depth buffer. LessEqual is standard. Always draws through everything (see-through-wall look).

tooltips.name: _ZWriteOverride
tooltips.text: Whether opaque geometry writes depth. On is correct for opaque; transparency modes manage this automatically, so leave at On unless hand-tuning.

tooltips.name: _ColorMask
tooltips.text: Which colour channels this material writes. RGBA is normal. None writes depth only (invisible but still occludes). Advanced use only.

tooltips.name: _OffsetFactor
tooltips.text: Slope-scaled depth bias. Negative pulls the surface toward the camera to beat z-fighting on coplanar decals.

tooltips.name: _OffsetUnits
tooltips.text: Constant depth bias. Pairs with Offset Factor. 0 is off.

tooltips.name: _ProxMin
tooltips.text: Distance at which the avatar starts fading as a camera approaches.

tooltips.name: _ProxMax
tooltips.text: Distance at which the avatar is fully faded. Must be larger than the start.

tooltips.name: _ALEnvRelease
tooltips.text: How long reactions take to fall after a beat. Low is snappy and percussive, high holds and glides. Attack is always fast.

tooltips.name: _VertALMask
tooltips.text: Limits the motion to white areas. Sampled per vertex, so it needs reasonable vertex density to read a detailed mask.

tooltips.name: _VertALTransMin
tooltips.text: Offset in object space when the band is silent.

tooltips.name: _VertALTransMax
tooltips.text: Offset in object space when the band is at full intensity.

tooltips.name: _VertALWTransMin
tooltips.text: World-aligned offset when the band is silent. Stays world-up etc. no matter how the avatar is rotated.

tooltips.name: _VertALWTransMax
tooltips.text: World-aligned offset at full band intensity.

tooltips.name: _VertALRot
tooltips.text: Rotation per axis around the object pivot. In Intensity mode this is the angle at full band. In Accumulate modes it is degrees per audio-second (keeps turning, faster when the band is active).

tooltips.name: _VertALRotModeX
tooltips.text: Intensity rotates by band level and returns. Accumulate keeps turning while the band is active (Chronotensity, no snap-back). Accumulate When Quiet turns when the band is silent. Ping Pong bounces between 0 and full.

tooltips.name: _VertALRotSpd
tooltips.text: Continuous spin per axis. Rate scales with band intensity via Chronotensity, so it speeds up on the beat and coasts smoothly instead of jittering.

tooltips.name: _VertALScaleMin
tooltips.text: Object-pivot scale when the band is silent. 1,1,1 is unchanged.

tooltips.name: _VertALScaleMax
tooltips.text: Scale at full band intensity.

tooltips.name: _VertALUVMode
tooltips.text: Offset shifts the UV by band level and returns. Scroll keeps scrolling, faster when the band is active (Chronotensity).

tooltips.name: _VertALUVSpeed
tooltips.text: Offset mode: max UV shift at full band. Scroll mode: UV per audio-second.

tooltips.name: _MainTex
tooltips.text: Your main colour texture, the albedo.

tooltips.name: _BumpMap
tooltips.text: Tangent space normal map for surface detail.

tooltips.name: _BumpScale
tooltips.text: How strong the normal map reads. 1 is normal, 0 is flat.

tooltips.name: _AlphaMode
tooltips.text: Opaque is solid (alpha ignored). Cutout uses albedo alpha for hard-edged transparency like hair and lashes, with anti-aliased alpha-to-coverage edges. Transparent is true alpha blending for glass, ghosts, and fades. Switching this auto-sets blending, depth write, and render queue.

tooltips.name: _Cutoff
tooltips.text: Albedo alpha below this is cut away. Around 0.5 is typical.

tooltips.name: _AlphaSourceEnable
tooltips.text: Off uses the albedo texture's own alpha for transparency. On reads opacity from the dedicated map below instead, handy when your alpha lives in its own file or in a colour channel rather than the albedo alpha.

tooltips.name: _AlphaTex
tooltips.text: Dedicated opacity texture. White is opaque, black is clear. Choose which channel holds the opacity below. Shares the albedo's tiling and offset.

tooltips.name: _AlphaChannel
tooltips.text: Which channel of the map holds the opacity. A standalone grey opacity map is usually Red; an albedo+transparency export keeps it in Alpha.

tooltips.name: _Saturation
tooltips.text: Boosts or mutes all colours. 1 leaves them unchanged.

tooltips.name: _Brightness
tooltips.text: Multiplies overall brightness. 1 is unchanged.

tooltips.name: _Gamma
tooltips.text: Adjusts midtone contrast. 1 is unchanged.

tooltips.name: _BaseHueShift
tooltips.text: Rotates every hue by a fixed amount.

tooltips.name: _BaseHueShiftAL
tooltips.text: Extra hue rotation driven by AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _BaseHueBand
tooltips.text: Which AudioLink band drives the hue shift.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Tex
tooltips.text: The decal image. Its alpha is the cutout. Place and size it with the Position and Size sliders below.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Color
tooltips.text: Multiplies the decal colour and alpha.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Opacity
tooltips.text: Overall decal opacity, 0 to 1. This is a plain slider (not a keyword), so it animates from an avatar menu - use it to fade a decal like blush in and out. 0 is invisible, 1 is full.

tooltips.name: _Decal0PosX
tooltips.text: Left-right placement across the UV. 0.5 is centre.

tooltips.name: _Decal0PosY
tooltips.text: Up-down placement across the UV. 0.5 is centre.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Scale
tooltips.text: How large the decal is in UV space. Smaller is a tighter patch.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Rotation
tooltips.text: Spins the decal in place, in degrees.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Blend
tooltips.text: Normal lays it on top. Add and Screen brighten. Multiply darkens.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Emit
tooltips.text: Makes the decal glow. 0 is a normal lit decal, higher adds bloom.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Overlay
tooltips.text: Draws this decal as a flat overlay on top of the interior room, screen, and lighting, instead of painting it onto the lit surface. Use this to layer logos or art over a room window.

tooltips.name: _Decal0Flipbook
tooltips.text: Treats the texture as a grid sprite sheet and plays the cells in sequence over time, like a GIF.

tooltips.name: _Decal0FlipCols
tooltips.text: Number of columns in the sprite sheet.

tooltips.name: _Decal0FlipRows
tooltips.text: Number of rows in the sprite sheet.

tooltips.name: _Decal0FlipFPS
tooltips.text: How many frames play per second.

tooltips.text: Enabling this compiles this slot's textures into the shader, so it recompiles once. Sliders and colours inside stay instant. Note: because this sets a shader keyword, animate Tint alpha for menu toggles rather than this checkbox.

tooltips.name: _DetailMask
tooltips.text: Where detail applies. White shows detail, black is the plain base.

tooltips.name: _DetailTiling
tooltips.text: Tiling of the detail maps. Detail typically tiles 4-16x over the base UVs.

tooltips.name: _DetailAlbedo
tooltips.text: Multiplied at 2x, so mid grey leaves the base unchanged, darker darkens, lighter lightens.

tooltips.name: _DetailAlbedoStrength
tooltips.text: How strongly the detail albedo blends in.

tooltips.name: _DetailNormal
tooltips.text: High-frequency normal blended over the base normal (whiteout blend).

tooltips.name: _DetailNormalStrength
tooltips.text: Strength of the detail normal. 0 is flat.

tooltips.name: _LightingModel
tooltips.text: Toon gives flat banded shading. Realistic gives smooth PBR style shading. Cloth uses a soft wrapped diffuse and a fabric sheen halo instead of a hard hotspot - velvet, wool, knits. Metal needs no mode of its own; use Realistic PBR with the metallic map.

tooltips.name: _ShadowEdge
tooltips.text: Where the toon shadow line sits. Lower puts more surface in shadow.

tooltips.name: _ShadowSoft
tooltips.text: How soft the toon shadow edge is. 0 is a hard line.

tooltips.name: _ShadowDither
tooltips.text: Adds a film-grain stipple across the shadow edge. Off by default. Meant to break up banding on a SOFT edge, so raise Shadow Softness alongside it; on a hard edge it just looks grainy.

tooltips.name: _SpecEdge
tooltips.text: How sharp the toon specular highlight edge is.

tooltips.name: _ClothWrap
tooltips.text: How far light wraps past the terminator. Fabric scatters light through its fibers, so cloth shades softer than a hard lambert. 0 is standard falloff.

tooltips.name: _SheenColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the fabric sheen halo at grazing angles. White for silk and satin, a dim tint of the base colour for wool and velvet. Smoothness controls how tight the halo is.

tooltips.name: _ShadowTint
tooltips.text: Colour multiplied into shadowed areas. Default is neutral grey; tint it cool or warm to taste.

tooltips.name: _MaxBrightness
tooltips.text: Caps how bright direct light can make the surface.

tooltips.name: _MinBrightness
tooltips.text: Raises the darkest the surface can get so it never goes fully black.

tooltips.name: _GrayscaleLighting
tooltips.text: Desaturates both the scene light and the ambient/world colour, keeping only brightness. Good for a neutral look or to kill a coloured-world tint. No effect when the lighting is already white.

tooltips.name: _ReceiveShadows
tooltips.text: Lets shadows cast by other objects land on this surface.

tooltips.name: _SSSMask
tooltips.text: Where scattering applies. White scatters, black shades normally. Paint this to skin only.

tooltips.name: _SSSTintMode
tooltips.text: What tints the scattered light. Custom uses the colour below. From Base Color derives the tint from the albedo, so one material adapts across skin tones automatically. Skin, Foliage, and Marble are ready-made looks.

tooltips.name: _SSSColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the scattered light. Warm red-orange reads as skin. Avoid fully saturated colours or coloured world lights get filtered to black.

tooltips.name: _SSSTermWidth
tooltips.text: Width of the warm band where light rolls into shadow. In Toon mode it hugs the Shadow Edge line.

tooltips.name: _SSSTermStrength
tooltips.text: Brightness of the warm terminator band. 0 turns the band off.

tooltips.name: _SSSThicknessMap
tooltips.text: Black lets light through (ears, fingers, nose wings); white blocks it. Bake one in Blender or Substance by inverting a through-mesh AO. Left empty, everything transmits and the SSS Mask does the limiting.

tooltips.name: _SSSTransStrength
tooltips.text: How much light bleeds through from behind. 0 turns transmission off.

tooltips.name: _SSSTransPower
tooltips.text: Sharpness of the glow around a light seen through the surface. Higher is a tighter hotspot.

tooltips.name: _SSSTransDistortion
tooltips.text: How much the surface normal bends the transmitted light, adding surface shape to the glow.

tooltips.name: _SSSAmbient
tooltips.text: Lets a little probe light through thin areas even with no direct light, so ears stay alive in probe-lit worlds. Flat and directionless; the slider below is the directional version.

tooltips.name: _SSSProbeLight
tooltips.text: Derives the dominant light direction from the world's light probes and runs it through the same focused transmission as a real light. This is how baked suns and club lighting - most VRChat worlds - get natural through-skin glow, and it makes Transmission Focus and Normal Distortion work in worlds with no realtime directional light. 0 is off.

tooltips.name: _SSSLTCGI
tooltips.text: Lets LTCGI screens and area lights shine through thin parts from behind, like a dancefloor screen glowing through ears. Still uses the Scatter Color, mask, thickness map, and Transmission Strength above; only Focus and Distortion do not apply, since area lights are already spatially shaped. Costs a second full LTCGI evaluation, so leave it off unless the avatar is headed for LTCGI club worlds. Needs the LTCGI System enabled at the bottom of this shader.

tooltips.name: _SSSLVDepth
tooltips.text: How far behind the surface, in metres, the Light Volume is sampled for transmission. The transmitted colour becomes the light actually present inside the body part, so an LV light tucked behind the ear shows through in that light's colour. Only active in Light Volume worlds with the Light Volumes System enabled.

tooltips.name: _BakedCubemap
tooltips.text: A cubemap used for reflections in worlds with no reflection probes.

tooltips.name: _FallbackCubemapStrength
tooltips.text: How much the fallback cubemap fills in when a world is dark.

tooltips.name: _ForceFallback
tooltips.text: Preview only. Always uses the fallback and ignores the world probe.

tooltips.name: _ReflStrength
tooltips.text: Scales all reflections. 0 is off, 1 is normal, 2 is punchy. Roughness still blurs them.

tooltips.name: _PackMode
tooltips.text: How to read the Packed Map. ZFS Packed uses R=Metallic, G=AO, B=Smoothness. Unity MetallicSmoothness (the format most prepacked maps ship in) uses R=Metallic and Alpha=Smoothness with no AO channel - pick this if your surface renders black with a prepacked map.

tooltips.name: _PackedMap
tooltips.text: One texture holding three maps. Red metallic, green AO, blue smoothness.

tooltips.name: _InvSmooth
tooltips.text: Turn on if your blue channel is roughness instead of smoothness.

tooltips.name: _PackedTiling
tooltips.text: Tiling of the packed map across the surface.

tooltips.name: _PackedOffset
tooltips.text: Shifts the packed map across the surface.

tooltips.name: _PackedPan
tooltips.text: Scrolls the packed map over time.

tooltips.name: _PackedStochastic
tooltips.text: Hides obvious tiling repeats by randomising sampling. Slightly costlier.

tooltips.name: _Metallic
tooltips.text: Scales the map's red channel. With no map assigned this is simply the metalness. At 0 the surface is fully non-metal whatever the map says.

tooltips.name: _AdvancedRemap
tooltips.text: Adds floor sliders so a map can be remapped into a narrower range instead of scaled. Leave off unless you need it - a floor equal to the slider above pins every pixel to one value and the map stops doing anything.

tooltips.name: _MetallicMin
tooltips.text: Metalness where the map's red channel is black. Raises a weak map off zero. Equal to Metallic means the map is ignored entirely.

tooltips.name: _Smoothness
tooltips.text: Scales the map's smoothness channel. With no map assigned this is simply the smoothness.

tooltips.name: _SmoothnessMin
tooltips.text: Smoothness where the map's channel reads black. Raises a too-rough map. Equal to Smoothness means the map is ignored entirely.

tooltips.name: _OcclusionStrength
tooltips.text: How strongly the AO channel darkens crevices.

tooltips.name: _ReflTint
tooltips.text: Colour multiplied into reflections.

tooltips.name: _SpecTint
tooltips.text: Colour multiplied into the specular highlight.

tooltips.name: _AnisoColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the anisotropic streak.

tooltips.name: _AnisoDir
tooltips.text: Which surface axis the streak follows. Only used in Mesh Tangent mode.

tooltips.name: _AnisoDirMode
tooltips.text: Where the grain direction comes from. Object Space Map ignores UV seams.

tooltips.name: _AnisoFlowMap
tooltips.text: Used in Tangent Flow mode. RG paints grain direction in tangent space. R = along U, G = along V.

tooltips.name: _AnisoObjectMap
tooltips.text: Used in Object Space mode. RGB is a 3D grain direction baked in object space. Tangent independent so it ignores UV seams.

tooltips.name: _AnisoShift
tooltips.text: Slides the highlight along the grain direction.

tooltips.name: _AnisoPower
tooltips.text: Sharpness of the streak. Higher is tighter.

tooltips.name: _AnisoStrength
tooltips.text: Brightness of the anisotropic highlight.

tooltips.name: _AnisoMask
tooltips.text: Limits the effect to white areas. Paint it onto hair or metal only.

tooltips.name: _StyleSpecTint
tooltips.text: Colour of the stylized highlights.

tooltips.name: _StyleSpecUseLight
tooltips.text: Multiply the highlight by the scene light colour.

tooltips.name: _StyleSpecMask
tooltips.text: Limits the stylized highlights to white areas.

tooltips.text: A band that adds onto this layer brightness.

tooltips.name: _Em2AddAmt
tooltips.text: Strength of the additive band.

tooltips.name: _Em2MinEmiss
tooltips.text: Glow multiplier when the surface is in shadow.

tooltips.name: _Em2MaxEmiss
tooltips.text: Glow multiplier when the surface is fully lit.

tooltips.name: _Em2MinLight
tooltips.text: Lighting level treated as fully dark.

tooltips.name: _Em2MaxLight
tooltips.text: Lighting level treated as fully lit.

tooltips.name: _Em2BlinkSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast this layer blinks.

tooltips.name: _Em2BlinkMin
tooltips.text: How dim the bottom of each blink gets. 0 blinks fully off.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanDir
tooltips.text: Vertical sweeps up and down. Horizontal sweeps side to side like a scanner.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanMode
tooltips.text: Loop jumps back to the start each cycle. Ping Pong bounces back and forth.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the band travels.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanWidth
tooltips.text: Thickness of the moving band, in UV.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanSoft
tooltips.text: How soft the band edges are. 0 is a hard edge.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanFloor
tooltips.text: How much the rest of the mask still glows. 0 shows only the band, 1 disables the sweep.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanPixels
tooltips.text: Quantizes the band into chunky blocks for a retro 32-bit look. 0 is smooth.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScanGlitch
tooltips.text: Randomly flickers pixels in the band on and off for a glitchy look. 0 is steady. Needs a pixel grid, so it falls back to 64 blocks if Pixelation is 0.

tooltips.name: _Em2Triplanar
tooltips.text: Project the mirror pattern in 3D instead of by UV.

tooltips.name: _Em2Rotation
tooltips.text: Rotates the mirror pattern.

tooltips.name: _Em2BgColor
tooltips.text: Tint of the infinity mirror background.

tooltips.name: _Em2ScaleLock
tooltips.text: Lock the background to a uniform scale using the X value.

tooltips.name: _Em2BgScale
tooltips.text: Scale of the background pattern.

tooltips.name: _Em2TileX
tooltips.text: Repeat the background horizontally.

tooltips.name: _Em2TileY
tooltips.text: Repeat the background vertically.

tooltips.name: _Em2Pan
tooltips.text: Scrolls the background over time.

tooltips.name: _Em2Layers
tooltips.text: How many repeating depth layers the mirror draws.

tooltips.name: _Em2Parallax
tooltips.text: Starting depth of the first mirror layer.

tooltips.name: _Em2LayerDist
tooltips.text: Gap between each mirror layer.

tooltips.name: _Em2NearBright
tooltips.text: Brightness of the closest mirror layer.

tooltips.name: _Em2FarBright
tooltips.text: Brightness of the deepest mirror layer.

tooltips.name: _Em3Enable
tooltips.text: Enabling this compiles this slot's textures into the shader, so it recompiles once. Sliders and colours inside stay instant. Note: because this sets a shader keyword, animate Emission Intensity for menu toggles rather than this checkbox.

tooltips.name: _Em3Mask
tooltips.text: Where this layer glows. White glows, black does not.

tooltips.name: _Em3Color
tooltips.text: Glow colour. Push the HDR intensity up for bloom.

tooltips.name: _Em3Intensity
tooltips.text: Overall brightness multiplier for this layer.

tooltips.name: _Em3Hue
tooltips.text: Rotates this layer hue with AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _Em3Mode
tooltips.text: How the audio drives the glow pattern. Gradient Path makes the audio travel along this slot's Path Gradient map.

tooltips.name: _Em3PathTex
tooltips.text: Grayscale gradient for this slot's Gradient Path mode. Paint a black-to-white ramp along the route the audio should travel - trim lines, cables, tattoos. Audio enters at black and flows toward white. Import with sRGB off for even flow.

tooltips.name: _Em3Base
tooltips.text: Baseline glow always on, before audio adds to it.

tooltips.name: _Em3EdgeGlow
tooltips.text: Adds extra glow along the silhouette edges.

tooltips.name: _Em3EdgePower
tooltips.text: How tight the edge glow band is.

tooltips.name: _Em3Band
tooltips.text: Main AudioLink band this layer reacts to.

tooltips.name: _Em3AL
tooltips.text: How much the chosen band boosts brightness.

tooltips.name: _Em3PulseScale
tooltips.text: Spacing of the rings in the center out pulse modes.

tooltips.name: _Em3Center
tooltips.text: UV point the pulse radiates from.

tooltips.name: _Em3VolBoost
tooltips.text: Also brighten with overall track volume.

tooltips.name: _Em3VolAmt
tooltips.text: How much overall volume adds brightness.

tooltips.name: _Em3MultBand
tooltips.text: A band that multiplies this layer brightness.

tooltips.name: _Em3MultAmt
tooltips.text: Strength of the multiplier band.

tooltips.name: _Em3AddBand
tooltips.text: A band that adds onto this layer brightness.

tooltips.name: _Em3AddAmt
tooltips.text: Strength of the additive band.

tooltips.name: _Em3MaxEmiss

tooltips.name: _Em3MinLight
tooltips.text: Lighting level treated as fully dark.

tooltips.name: _Em3MaxLight
tooltips.text: Lighting level treated as fully lit.

tooltips.name: _Em3BlinkSpeed

tooltips.name: _Em3BlinkMin

tooltips.name: _Em3ScanDir
tooltips.text: Vertical sweeps up and down. Horizontal sweeps side to side like a scanner.

tooltips.name: _Em3ScanSoft

tooltips.text: Starting depth of the first mirror layer.

tooltips.name: _Em3LayerDist
tooltips.text: Gap between each mirror layer.

tooltips.text: Brightness of the closest mirror layer.
