tooltips.name: _RoomCube
tooltips.text: A cubemap of the room interior. Plus Z faces the back wall, plus and minus Y are ceiling and floor.

tooltips.name: _RoomMask
tooltips.text: Where the window appears. White shows the room, black keeps the normal surface.

tooltips.name: _RoomColor
tooltips.text: Tints and brightens the room. Push HDR for a glowing interior.

tooltips.name: _RoomDepth
tooltips.text: How deep the room recedes. Higher looks like a larger, deeper space.

tooltips.name: _RoomTile
tooltips.text: How many room cells span the mask. 1 is a single room.

tooltips.name: _RoomScrollX
tooltips.text: Rotates the room view left or right over time, like turning inside the box. Seamless loop. 0 is static.

tooltips.name: _RoomScrollY
tooltips.text: Rotates the room view up or down over time. Seamless loop. 0 is static.

tooltips.name: _RoomSlideX
tooltips.text: Slides the whole room sideways over time. Loops by repeating, so it reads cleanest with symmetric or tiling room cubemaps. 0 is static.

tooltips.name: _RoomSlideY
tooltips.text: Slides the whole room up or down over time. Loops by repeating. 0 is static.

tooltips.name: _RoomEdge
tooltips.text: Sharpness of the window mask edge. Low is a crisp cut. If the room looks milky or washed out, your mask is not pure white inside; keep this low and it cleans up by forcing the inside fully opaque.

tooltips.name: _RoomGlassWarp
tooltips.text: How strongly the glass bends the view of the interior. 0 is perfectly flat glass.

tooltips.name: _RoomGlassChroma
tooltips.text: Prismatic red and blue split through the glass, strongest where the view bends most. 0 is none.

tooltips.name: _RoomDepthMode
tooltips.text: None keeps walls even. Fog darkens far walls. Dream Haze dissolves them into a soft glowing mist for a fantasy look.

tooltips.name: _RoomFade
tooltips.text: How strongly the fog or haze builds with depth.

tooltips.name: _RoomHazeColor
tooltips.text: Colour the far depths glow with in Dream Haze mode. Push HDR for a brighter mist.

tooltips.name: _RoomSoften
tooltips.text: Blurs the room with depth for a dreamy, out of focus feel. 0 is crisp. Needs the cubemap to have mipmaps.

tooltips.name: _RoomALEnable
tooltips.text: Pulse the room brightness with a frequency band.

tooltips.name: _RoomBand
tooltips.text: Frequency band that drives the room.

tooltips.name: _RoomAL
tooltips.text: How much the band brightens the room.

tooltips.name: _RefractMask
tooltips.text: Where the glass shows. White is full refraction, black is the normal surface.

tooltips.name: _RefractStrength
tooltips.text: How strongly the surface bends what is behind it.

tooltips.name: _RefractCA
tooltips.text: Splits red and blue for a prismatic glass edge. 0 is none.

tooltips.name: _RefractTint
tooltips.text: Tints the refracted result. White is clear glass.

tooltips.name: _RefractBlend
tooltips.text: Blends between the surface and the refracted view. 1 is fully see through.

tooltips.name: _RefractMap
tooltips.text: A normal or noise map that adds moving shimmer on top of the surface distortion. Leave default for plain glass.

tooltips.name: _RefractTile
tooltips.text: Tiling of the shimmer map.

tooltips.name: _RefractScroll
tooltips.text: Scrolls the shimmer map for a flowing heat haze. 0 is static.

tooltips.name: _RefractALEnable
tooltips.text: Pulse the distortion strength with a frequency band.

tooltips.name: _RefractBand
tooltips.text: Band that drives the wobble.

tooltips.name: _RefractAL
tooltips.text: How much the band adds to the distortion.

tooltips.name: _ScreenMask
tooltips.text: Where the screen shows. White is screen, black is the normal surface.

tooltips.name: _ScreenMode
tooltips.text: Oscilloscope draws the live waveform. EQ Bars shows four frequency band levels as LED columns.

tooltips.name: _ScreenLineColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the waveform or bars.

tooltips.name: _ScreenWaveAmp
tooltips.text: Height of the oscilloscope trace.

tooltips.name: _ScreenWaveSamples
tooltips.text: How many waveform samples span the screen width.

tooltips.name: _ScreenLineWidth
tooltips.text: Thickness of the oscilloscope line.

tooltips.name: _ScreenArt
tooltips.text: A still image drawn behind the wave. Strength below.

tooltips.name: _ScreenArtStrength
tooltips.text: Brightness of the screen art.

tooltips.name: _ScreenBackdrop
tooltips.text: Grayscale gradient backdrop, tinted by Background Tint. Use Tiling and Offset to pick an atlas quadrant.

tooltips.name: _ScreenBGColor
tooltips.text: Colour the backdrop is tinted to.

tooltips.name: _ScreenGridProc
tooltips.text: Draws the grid analytically with anti aliasing, no moire at any distance. Off uses a grid texture instead.

tooltips.name: _ScreenGridCells
tooltips.text: How many grid cells span the screen.

tooltips.name: _ScreenGridLineW
tooltips.text: Thickness of the grid lines.

tooltips.name: _ScreenGridMinor
tooltips.text: Strength of the finer sub grid.

tooltips.name: _ScreenGridTex
tooltips.text: Used only when Procedural Grid is off.

tooltips.name: _ScreenGridColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the grid lines.

tooltips.name: _ScreenGridStrength
tooltips.text: Overall grid brightness.

tooltips.name: _ScreenLCDTex
tooltips.text: Tile this high (e.g. 80 by 80). Up close the screen resolves into RGB subpixels.

tooltips.name: _ScreenLCDStrength
tooltips.text: How strong the subpixel filter is. 0 is off.

tooltips.name: _ScreenScanline
tooltips.text: Strength of the CRT scanlines.

tooltips.name: _ScreenScanCount
tooltips.text: How many scanlines down the screen.

tooltips.name: _ScreenBSOD
tooltips.text: Replaces the screen with the crash image.

tooltips.name: _ScreenBSODNoAL
tooltips.text: Automatically show the crash image when there is no audio signal.

tooltips.name: _ScreenBSODTex
tooltips.text: Image shown in crash mode.

tooltips.name: _RimState
tooltips.text: Rim behaviour mode.

tooltips.name: _RimColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the edge glow.

tooltips.name: _RimHueShift
tooltips.text: Shifts the rim hue with AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _RimWidth
tooltips.text: How far the rim reaches in from the silhouette.

tooltips.name: _RimSoft
tooltips.text: How soft the rim falloff is.

tooltips.name: _RimBase
tooltips.text: Rim brightness, always on regardless of audio. Around 0.15 is a soft rim, 1 is normal, 2 is bright. In Audio Reactive mode the audio adds on top of this.

tooltips.name: _RimBand
tooltips.text: AudioLink band that drives the rim.

tooltips.name: _RimAL
tooltips.text: How much the band boosts the rim.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerMask
tooltips.text: Gradient shaping where ripples appear and how strong.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerMaskBlur
tooltips.text: Softens the gradient so the rings stay round and the starburst spikes on small speakers go away. 0 is sharp.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the ripple waves.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerState
tooltips.text: Ripple behaviour mode.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerHueShift
tooltips.text: Shifts the ripple hue with AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerIntensity
tooltips.text: How far the ripples push forward off the surface.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerExpansion
tooltips.text: Lifts rings off the surface along the normal as they travel, for a domed pop. 0 keeps them flat on the speaker.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerRings
tooltips.text: Max rings in flight at once. In Audio Reactive mode this is how many recent beats stay visible; in Always On it is how many clock rings cycle. Max 6.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the ripples travel.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerRingThickness
tooltips.text: Solid width of each ring. Small values give thin crisp rings.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerRingSoftness
tooltips.text: Feathered fade added to the outer edge. Does not hollow the ring.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerThreshold
tooltips.text: How hard the band must rise to emit a ring. A ring launches the moment the band crosses this from below, and re-arms once it dips under about 60 percent of it, so one hit emits exactly one ring even through sustained bass. Raise it to pick out only the hardest hits.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerDirection
tooltips.text: Outward grows rings from the speaker center to the edge. Inward reverses it. Flip this if your rings travel the wrong way.

tooltips.name: _SpeakerBand
tooltips.text: AudioLink band that triggers the ripples.

tooltips.name: _EQMask
tooltips.text: Area the equalizer bars draw inside.

tooltips.name: _EQColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the EQ bars.

tooltips.name: _EQColumns
tooltips.text: How many frequency bars to show.

tooltips.name: _EQGain
tooltips.text: Boosts the spectrum into the visible range. The raw DFT is much quieter than the autogained band data, so this defaults well above 1.

tooltips.name: _EQCurve
tooltips.text: Below 1 lifts quiet frequencies for a log-style EQ look, like a music player. 1 is linear.

tooltips.name: _IridMask
tooltips.text: Where the iridescence shows.

tooltips.name: _IridColor1
tooltips.text: One of the three colours cycled in the oil slick shift.

tooltips.name: _IridColor2
tooltips.text: One of the three colours cycled in the oil slick shift.

tooltips.name: _IridColor3
tooltips.text: One of the three colours cycled in the oil slick shift.

tooltips.name: _IridThickness
tooltips.text: How quickly the gradient cycles across the viewing angle, in the Gradient model.

tooltips.name: _IridSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the colours drift on their own.

tooltips.name: _IridBand
tooltips.text: Which frequency band drives the iridescence.

tooltips.name: _IridAL
tooltips.text: How strongly the audio shifts the colours. In Thin Film this physically changes the film thickness, so the whole palette moves rather than just brightening.

tooltips.name: _DissolveColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the glowing burn edge.

tooltips.name: _DissolveHueShift
tooltips.text: Shifts the burn hue with AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _DissolveTex
tooltips.text: Grayscale noise pattern that decides the order pixels burn away. This is required for a gradual dissolve: assign a cloud or Perlin noise texture. Left empty (plain white) the whole surface vanishes at once instead of eating away.

tooltips.name: _DissolveAmount
tooltips.text: How much of the surface has burned away. 0 is fully intact, 100 is fully gone.

tooltips.name: _DissolveAL
tooltips.text: How much audio drives the dissolve amount.

tooltips.name: _DissolveWidth
tooltips.text: Thickness of the glowing burn edge that leads the dissolve.

tooltips.name: _DissolveBand
tooltips.text: AudioLink band that drives the burn.

tooltips.name: _OutlineMask
tooltips.text: Where the outline is allowed to draw.

tooltips.name: _OutlineState
tooltips.text: Outline behaviour mode.

tooltips.name: _OutlineColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the outline.

tooltips.name: _OutlineHueShift
tooltips.text: Shifts the outline hue with AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _OutlineFloat
tooltips.text: How far the hologram outline hovers off the mesh.

tooltips.name: _OutlineRGBSplit
tooltips.text: Amount of chromatic split in the outline.

tooltips.name: _OutlineSpread
tooltips.text: Thickness of the outline.

tooltips.name: _OutlineSlices
tooltips.text: How many broken blocks the outline splits into.

tooltips.name: _OutlineSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the outline jitters.

tooltips.name: _OutlineBand
tooltips.text: AudioLink band that drives the outline.

tooltips.name: _OutlineAL
tooltips.text: Gain on the band before it drives the outline. In Audio Reactive mode the band level sets brightness, jitter, and RGB split all at once, so without boost the effect can never exceed the raw band level. Raise this so beats saturate to the full always-on look; high values act like a gate.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdColor
tooltips.text: Flat colour of the outline shell.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdWidth
tooltips.text: Thickness of the outline. Read as metres in World mode, or on-screen scale in Screen mode.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdWidthMode
tooltips.text: World keeps a fixed thickness in metres, so it thins with distance. Screen keeps a constant on-screen thickness at any distance, the usual anime look.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdMask
tooltips.text: Where the outline is allowed to grow. White draws the outline, black removes it. Paint the face white-to-black to thin or drop the outline there.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdVColorMask
tooltips.text: Multiplies the outline width by a vertex-colour channel, so you can paint where the outline shows right in Unity with a vertex painter like Polybrush (free, Unity Package Manager). Stacks with the mask texture above. Best for knocking the outline off the face. White vertex = full outline, black = none.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdVColorChannel
tooltips.text: Which painted vertex-colour channel to read as the outline mask.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdTexTint
tooltips.text: Blends the outline toward the albedo colour. 0 is a flat colour, 1 multiplies the outline by the texture for a coloured ink look.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdLit
tooltips.text: On, the outline darkens in shadow and picks up the light colour. Off, it stays a flat colour everywhere.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdDistFade
tooltips.text: EXPERIMENTAL. Thins the outline as the viewer moves away, which hides the shell flaps that open up around hard edges like eyes and nostrils at distance. Tune the near/far range below. May interact oddly with very large or non-uniformly scaled avatars.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdFadeNear
tooltips.text: Within this camera distance the outline stays full width.

tooltips.name: _OutlineStdFadeFar
tooltips.text: Beyond this camera distance the outline has thinned to nothing. Should be larger than the near distance.

tooltips.name: _StarMask
tooltips.text: Optional. White shows the effect, black hides it. Leave it empty to apply the starfield across the whole material, or paint a mask to confine it, like a window into space.

tooltips.name: _ConstellationBlend
tooltips.text: How the whole constellation composites onto the surface. Add glows (the default), Screen glows more gently, Multiply and Darken tint or sink it into the surface, Overlay contrasts, Replace paints it on flat with no glow.

tooltips.name: _StarUVSource
tooltips.text: Which coordinate space the stars and nebula live in. UV0 maps to the mesh UVs and stretches with them. Panosphere projects onto a sphere around the view, so the field reads like real sky seen through the surface. Polar wraps it into rings. The mask still uses UV0 either way.

tooltips.name: _ConstellationEmission
tooltips.text: Master brightness for the entire constellation, applied before it blends onto the surface. Scales stars, lines, and nebula together.

tooltips.name: _StarBand
tooltips.text: Which frequency band the stars, lines, and nebula react to.

tooltips.name: _StarColorMode
tooltips.text: How star colour is chosen.

tooltips.name: _StarColor
tooltips.text: Base colour of the stars.

tooltips.name: _StarSaturation
tooltips.text: How saturated the star colours are.

tooltips.name: _StarAL
tooltips.text: How much audio peaks brighten the stars.

tooltips.name: _StarLayers
tooltips.text: How many parallax layers of stars.

tooltips.name: _StarDensity
tooltips.text: How many stars per area.

tooltips.name: _StarSize
tooltips.text: Size of each star.

tooltips.name: _StarScatter
tooltips.text: How far each star wanders from its cell centre. Low values line the stars up on a grid, which makes constellation lines look rectangular. Higher values scatter them so the lines connect at natural angles.

tooltips.name: _StarSoftness
tooltips.text: How soft the star dots are.

tooltips.name: _StarTwinkle
tooltips.text: How much the stars twinkle.

tooltips.name: _StarTwinkleSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast they twinkle.

tooltips.name: _StarSpeed
tooltips.text: Overall drift speed of the field.

tooltips.name: _StarDrift
tooltips.text: Adds chaotic jitter to the drift.

tooltips.name: _StarParallax
tooltips.text: Depth separation between star layers.

tooltips.name: _StarGlassWarp
tooltips.text: Distorts the starfield with a rippling glass wobble, like a window pane over space. 0 is flat. Pairs well with an emissive rim around the mask.

tooltips.name: _StarLineEnable
tooltips.text: Links nearby stars with faint lines. Stars on different layers drift at different speeds, so links stretch and reconnect on their own.

tooltips.name: _StarLineColorMode
tooltips.text: Line Color uses a single colour. Star Color gradients each link from its near star's colour to its far star's colour, following Star Color Mode.

tooltips.name: _StarLineColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the lines, used when Line Color Mode is set to Line Color.

tooltips.name: _StarLineStrength
tooltips.text: Overall line brightness. 0 hides the lines entirely.

tooltips.name: _StarLineThickness
tooltips.text: Line width, from thin hairlines to thick bars.

tooltips.name: _StarLineMaxLen
tooltips.text: Links longer than this fade out, so only nearby stars connect. Lower keeps the web sparse.

tooltips.name: _StarLineFade
tooltips.text: How sharply a link fades as it approaches the maximum length.

tooltips.name: _StarLineDepthFade
tooltips.text: How much deeper links dim so distance stays readable. 0 draws every link at full strength.

tooltips.name: _StarLineSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast each link shimmers. Each one is keyed to its own length and angle, so they pulse independently.

tooltips.name: _NebulaColorMode
tooltips.text: How the nebula colour is chosen. Base Color is a flat tint, ColorChord and Shifting Hue animate it, Gradient blends a four-stop gradient across the cloud, and Gradient Texture reads the colour from a ramp you supply.

tooltips.name: _StarBgColor
tooltips.text: Base colour of the nebula.

tooltips.name: _NebulaBright
tooltips.text: Overall brightness of the base nebula haze. Lower it so the AudioLink pop colour stands out more.

tooltips.name: _NebulaPopColor
tooltips.text: Colour the nebula flashes to on audio peaks.

tooltips.name: _NebGradColor0
tooltips.text: First gradient stop, anchored at position 0.

tooltips.name: _NebGradColor1
tooltips.text: Second gradient stop. Its position along the gradient is set by Color 2 Position.

tooltips.name: _NebGradColor2
tooltips.text: Third gradient stop. Its position along the gradient is set by Color 3 Position.

tooltips.name: _NebGradColor3
tooltips.text: Fourth gradient stop, anchored at position 1.

tooltips.name: _NebGradPos1
tooltips.text: Where the second colour sits along the gradient, between the first and third stops.

tooltips.name: _NebGradPos2
tooltips.text: Where the third colour sits along the gradient, between the second and fourth stops.

tooltips.name: _NebGradTex
tooltips.text: A horizontal ramp texture read left to right across the nebula. Used when Nebula Color Mode is Gradient Texture.

tooltips.name: _NebulaAL
tooltips.text: How sensitive the nebula pop is to audio.

tooltips.name: _RaymarchSteps
tooltips.text: Raymarch quality. Higher looks better but costs more.

tooltips.name: _RaymarchDensity
tooltips.text: How thick the volumetric fog is.

tooltips.name: _MaskTex
tooltips.text: White areas break apart. Black areas stay solid.

tooltips.name: _EmissionColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the glow added by the break.

tooltips.name: _BreakStyle
tooltips.text: Preset look. Full Energy fills the gap with glow. Glowing Fragments leaves an empty gap.

tooltips.name: _BreakManual
tooltips.text: Override the preset and hand tune the glow sliders.

tooltips.name: _BreakGlow
tooltips.text: Glow on the broken surface faces.

tooltips.name: _BreakCoreGlow
tooltips.text: Glow filling the inner gap between pieces.

tooltips.name: _BreakFade
tooltips.text: Dissolves the broken pieces to transparent as they separate.

tooltips.name: _BreakHueShift
tooltips.text: Shifts the break glow hue with AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _BreakMode
tooltips.text: Splinter Wave gives per-triangle shards: each piece moves independently and the mask is read at full detail. Pixel Grid snaps everything to a coarse cell grid, so pieces inside a cell move together as cubes and the mask is sampled per cell (detail is lost by design). Use Splinter Wave for smooth, mask-accurate breaks.

tooltips.name: _BreakDrive
tooltips.text: Audio Beat triggers on the music. Slow Float drifts on its own.

tooltips.name: _FloatSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the slow float cycle runs.

tooltips.name: _FloatReach
tooltips.text: How far the float break opens at its peak.

tooltips.name: _FloatStagger
tooltips.text: How out of sync the pieces are. Low keeps them together.

tooltips.name: _FloatAudio
tooltips.text: Lets audio nudge the float amount.

tooltips.name: _Band
tooltips.text: AudioLink band that triggers the break.

tooltips.name: _Threshold
tooltips.text: How strong the audio must be to trigger a break.

tooltips.name: _GridSize
tooltips.text: How fine the cubes are in Pixel Grid mode.

tooltips.name: _Tessellation
tooltips.text: Subdivides the mesh for finer breaks. Costs performance.

tooltips.name: _TessNear
tooltips.text: Distance within which full tessellation detail is kept.

tooltips.name: _TessFar
tooltips.text: Distance beyond which tessellation turns off.

tooltips.name: _WaveBottom
tooltips.text: Where the splinter wave starts, in metres.

tooltips.name: _WaveTop
tooltips.text: Where the splinter wave ends, in metres.

tooltips.name: _RiseHeight
tooltips.text: How far pieces rise as they break.

tooltips.name: _Spread
tooltips.text: How far pieces pop outward.

tooltips.name: _Jitter
tooltips.text: Random floating drift of the pieces.

tooltips.name: _Shrink
tooltips.text: How much pieces shrink as they break.

tooltips.name: _Tumble
tooltips.text: How much pieces spin as they break.

tooltips.name: _EdgeWidth
tooltips.text: Width of the glowing rim on the broken edges.

tooltips.name: _EdgeGap
tooltips.text: Pushes pieces apart to open gaps.

tooltips.name: _HeatGlow
tooltips.text: Glow that builds up just before a break.

tooltips.name: _CoreTiling
tooltips.text: Tiling of the inner core pattern.

tooltips.name: _CoreDepth
tooltips.text: Parallax depth of the inner core.

tooltips.name: _CoreTex
tooltips.text: Pattern shown on the inner faces of broken pieces.

tooltips.name: _GlitterColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the flakes. Push HDR up for bloom.

tooltips.name: _GlitterMask
tooltips.text: Where the glitter shows. White shows, black hides.

tooltips.name: _GlitterDensity
tooltips.text: How many flakes. Higher packs them tighter.

tooltips.name: _GlitterSize
tooltips.text: How big each flake is.

tooltips.name: _GlitterBrightness
tooltips.text: Overall sparkle intensity.

tooltips.name: _GlitterAmount
tooltips.text: How many flakes are lit at once. Higher sparkles more.

tooltips.name: _GlitterViewRange
tooltips.text: How wide an angle a flake stays visible. Low gives sharp glints that pop in and out, high shows more at once.

tooltips.name: _GlitterSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the flakes twinkle.

tooltips.name: _GlitterFlow
tooltips.text: Scrolls the flake field in a direction over time.

tooltips.name: _GlitterProjection
tooltips.text: UV follows the texture layout. World Triplanar keeps flake size even and ignores UV seams.

tooltips.name: _GlitterLit
tooltips.text: On, the sparkle only shows where light hits. Off, it shows everywhere at full brightness.

tooltips.name: _GlitterALEnable
tooltips.text: Pulse the sparkle with the music.

tooltips.name: _GlitterBand
tooltips.text: Which frequency band drives the sparkle.

tooltips.name: _GlitterAL
tooltips.text: How much the band boosts the sparkle.

tooltips.name: _GlitchMask
tooltips.text: Where the glitch displacement happens.

tooltips.name: _GlitchBand
tooltips.text: AudioLink band that drives the glitch.

tooltips.name: _GlitchThreshold
tooltips.text: How strong the audio must be to glitch.

tooltips.name: _GlitchIntensity
tooltips.text: How far blocks are displaced.

tooltips.name: _GlitchSlices
tooltips.text: How many blocks the mesh breaks into.

tooltips.name: _GlitchRGBSplit
tooltips.text: Chromatic split amount on the glitched UVs.

tooltips.name: _GlitchHue
tooltips.text: Brightness of the neon tint on glitched blocks.

tooltips.name: _HeightMap
tooltips.text: Shared black and white height map. Feeds both Height-to-Normal and Parallax below. White is high.

tooltips.name: _HeightStrength
tooltips.text: How deep the height detail reads.

tooltips.name: _ParallaxMask
tooltips.text: Where parallax is applied.

tooltips.name: _ParallaxStrength
tooltips.text: How much apparent depth the parallax adds.

tooltips.name: _ParallaxOffset
tooltips.text: Shifts the zero height level.

tooltips.name: _ParallaxMipBias
tooltips.text: Biases texture sharpness inside the parallax.

tooltips.name: _LTCGI
tooltips.text: Enables LTCGI area light support and sets the LTCGI shader keyword. Needs the LTCGI package in the project.

tooltips.name: _LTCGIStrength
tooltips.text: How strongly LTCGI area lights affect the avatar.

tooltips.name: _LTCGITintOn
tooltips.text: Multiply LTCGI diffuse and specular by a colour, to warm or cool the light from world screens.

tooltips.name: _LTCGIDiffuseTint
tooltips.text: Colour multiplied into the LTCGI diffuse contribution.

tooltips.name: _LTCGISpecularTint
tooltips.text: Colour multiplied into the LTCGI specular contribution.

tooltips.name: _LTCGIOcclusion
tooltips.text: How strongly baked AO darkens LTCGI. 0 ignores AO (screens light crevices freely), 1 applies it fully.

tooltips.name: _LightVolumes
tooltips.text: Enables VRC Light Volumes support and sets its shader keyword. Safe to leave on - it falls back to normal light probes in worlds without volumes.

tooltips.name: _LightVolumesStrength
tooltips.text: Scales the Light Volume ambient and speculars. 1 matches normal probe brightness in fallback.

tooltips.name: _LightVolumesSpec
tooltips.text: Approximate specular highlights from the volume data, so point and area Light Volume lights put real highlights on the avatar. Adds a little cost.

tooltips.name: _LVPointShading
tooltips.text: How strongly Point Light Volumes are shaped by the surface normal. Only used when VRC Light Volumes 3.x or newer is installed - on 2.x the shader calls an overload that has no shading and this does nothing. 0 disables per-surface shading, 1 is the standard smooth gradient, higher is sharper. Leave at 1 unless you want a harder falloff: LV 3.x's own default when the argument is omitted is 3, which is what makes lighting snap between areas.

tooltips.name: _DebugView
tooltips.text: Renders one lighting term on its own instead of the finished surface. Ambient covers indirect light including Light Volumes, and is the one to check first when a surface renders black; AO is the second, since it multiplies both ambient and reflections. Direct is realtime lights only. Reflection is the probe and fallback cubemap contribution after metallic and smoothness are applied. Set back to Off before locking - Off strips the feature from the locked shader, anything else ships it.

tooltips.name: _VRSLGI
tooltips.text: Reads the VRSL GI light data the world publishes. In worlds without it the light count reads zero and the loop never runs, so leaving this on is safe.

tooltips.name: _VRSLGIStrength
tooltips.text: Overall brightness of VRSL GI lights on this material.

tooltips.name: _VRSLGISpecular
tooltips.text: Adds specular highlights from each VRSL light, using this material's own smoothness and F0 tint rather than a separate set of controls.

tooltips.name: _VRSLGISpecularClamp
tooltips.text: Ceiling on any single light's specular. Stage rigs are bright and close; without a clamp a moving head sweeping past blows out to white.

tooltips.name: _VRSLGIToon
tooltips.text: Hard terminator instead of a smooth lambert gradient, so rig lighting matches a toon base rather than dropping realistic shading onto flat art.

tooltips.name: _VRSLGIOcclusion
tooltips.text: How much the AO map darkens VRSL GI contribution.

tooltips.name: _HoloEnable
tooltips.text: Turns the whole hologram overlay on. Adds scanlines, rim glow, a sweep bar, flicker, glitch, and a see-through look on top of the finished surface.

tooltips.name: _HoloColor
tooltips.text: The hologram's colour. Everything the effect adds (scanlines, rim, sweep) is tinted with it, and the surface is pulled toward it by Tint Amount.

tooltips.name: _HoloTintAmount
tooltips.text: How far the avatar's own colours collapse toward the Holo Color. 0 keeps the original colours, 1 goes fully monochrome.

tooltips.name: _HoloTransStyle
tooltips.text: How the see-through look is produced. True Alpha is real transparency and looks best, but needs the material's Transparency Mode set to a transparent option. Dither clips pixels in a fine pattern so it reads see-through in any render mode with no queue change.

tooltips.name: _HoloOpacity
tooltips.text: Base see-through amount. Bright scanlines, rim, and sweep push opacity back up locally, so the lit bands stay solid while flat areas fade.

tooltips.name: _HoloScanDensity
tooltips.text: How many scanlines run across the body. Measured in the avatar's own space, so very large or very small avatars may want this retuned.

tooltips.name: _HoloScanSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the scanlines scroll along the body.

tooltips.name: _HoloScanSharpness
tooltips.text: Line shape. Low is soft wide bands, high is thin crisp lines.

tooltips.name: _HoloScanStrength
tooltips.text: Brightness of the scanlines.

tooltips.name: _HoloRimStrength
tooltips.text: Brightness of the fresnel edge glow that haloes the silhouette.

tooltips.name: _HoloRimPower
tooltips.text: Width of the rim. Low spreads the glow inward, high keeps it to a thin edge.

tooltips.name: _HoloSweepStrength
tooltips.text: Brightness of the bright bar that travels up the body.

tooltips.name: _HoloSweepSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the sweep bar cycles up the body.

tooltips.name: _HoloSweepWidth
tooltips.text: Thickness of the sweep bar.

tooltips.name: _HoloFlicker
tooltips.text: Amount of brightness flutter, for an unstable-projection feel. 0 is steady.

tooltips.name: _HoloGlitchAmount
tooltips.text: Amount of horizontal tearing that jolts bands of the scanlines sideways.

tooltips.name: _HoloGlitchSpeed
tooltips.text: How often the glitch tears fire.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaEnable
tooltips.text: Turns on the plasma hits: audio-reactive flashes with expanding ripples that also bump the surface. Reacts to AudioLink.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaSites
tooltips.text: How many hit sites are scattered over the avatar. They cycle through the four audio bands, so more sites means more of the spectrum is represented.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColorMode
tooltips.text: How hit colours are chosen. Random Per Site gives each hit a fresh random colour. Fixed Color makes every hit one colour. Per Hit gives each hit slot its own colour (Hit 1, Hit 2, ...), and the number of slots follows Hit Sites.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor
tooltips.text: The colour used for every hit when Color Mode is Fixed Color.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaGlow
tooltips.text: Overall brightness of the hits and ripples.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaRippleDist
tooltips.text: How far each hit reaches before it fades.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaHitSize
tooltips.text: Size of the bright flash at the moment a hit lands.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaDisplace
tooltips.text: How strongly the geometry reacts. In Ripple it is the surface bump height; in Shatter it is how far the shards break apart. The shard look itself (rise, tumble, shrink, gap) comes from the Geometry Break advanced settings.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaRate
tooltips.text: How fast each hit slot relocates and re-fires. Higher means hits pop more often at new spots. Roughly, one ripple per hit per 1/Rate seconds.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaRingWidth
tooltips.text: Thickness of the expanding ring, in the Ripple style.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaThreshold
tooltips.text: Audio level a band must exceed before its hits show. Raise it to ignore quiet passages and the AudioLink noise floor so it stays dark until the music hits.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaSpread
tooltips.text: How far across the avatar's own 3D space the hits scatter. Tune to your avatar's size so hits land on the body.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor1
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 1, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor2
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 2, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor3
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 3, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor4
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 4, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor5
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 5, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor6
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 6, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor7
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 7, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaColor8
tooltips.text: Colour for hit slot 8, used in the Per Hit colour mode.

tooltips.name: _RetroEnable
tooltips.text: Turns on the PS1 retro look: vertex snap, pixelation, colour reduction, and scanlines.

tooltips.name: _RetroSnap
tooltips.text: Snaps vertices to a low virtual screen resolution, recreating the PS1's jittery, wobbly geometry.

tooltips.name: _RetroSnapRes
tooltips.text: The virtual resolution vertices snap to. Lower is chunkier and more jittery; 320 is the PS1 default.

tooltips.name: _RetroPixelate
tooltips.text: Snaps texture UVs to a coarse grid so textures look blocky, like low-resolution PS1 art.

tooltips.name: _RetroPixelRes
tooltips.text: How many texture blocks across. Lower is chunkier.

tooltips.name: _RetroLevels
tooltips.text: How many colour steps per channel the output is reduced to. 32 is the PS1's 5-bit colour; lower bands harder.

tooltips.name: _RetroDither
tooltips.text: Strength of the ordered dither that hides the colour banding. 0 shows hard bands.

tooltips.name: _RetroScanlines
tooltips.text: Darkens alternating screen rows for a CRT look. 0 is off.

tooltips.name: _RetroScanCount
tooltips.text: How many scanlines run down the screen.

tooltips.name: _RetroAffine
tooltips.text: Interpolates the main UVs without perspective correction, so textures swim and warp like PS1 rendering, strongest on large triangles at grazing angles. Affects UV0-based textures (albedo, detail, parallax, packed maps); matcaps and world- or screen-projected effects keep their own mapping.

tooltips.name: _ViewVisEnable
tooltips.text: Lets this material be shown or hidden separately in normal view, mirrors, and cameras.

tooltips.name: _ViewVisDirect
tooltips.text: Show in normal rendering: your own direct view and how other players see you. Off hides it there while mirrors and cameras can still show it.

tooltips.name: _ViewVisMirror
tooltips.text: Show this material in mirrors.

tooltips.name: _ViewVisCamera
tooltips.text: Show this material in VRChat cameras and photos.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaIntensity
tooltips.text: Master fade for the whole effect. 1 is full, 0 is fully off. Drive this from a menu radial to smoothly fade the plasma in and out.

tooltips.name: _HoloIntensity
tooltips.text: Master fade for the whole hologram, including the see-through. 1 is full, 0 returns the surface to normal. Ideal for a menu radial.

tooltips.name: _EQIntensity
tooltips.text: Master fade for the EQ bars. 1 is full, 0 is fully off. Drive from a menu radial for a smooth fade.

tooltips.name: _MorphEnable
tooltips.text: Distorts the surface's texture coordinates for a swimming, melting, or glitching look.

tooltips.name: _MorphIntensity
tooltips.text: Master fade for the morph. 1 is full, 0 is fully off. Good for a menu radial.

tooltips.name: _MorphMode
tooltips.text: The distortion pattern. Wave is a smooth cross-ripple, Swirl twists around the centre, Pinch pulses in and out, Noise drifts organically like heat haze, and Jitter snaps in blocks for a digital glitch.

tooltips.name: _MorphStrength
tooltips.text: How far the coordinates are pushed. Small values read as a shimmer, large values smear the texture.

tooltips.name: _MorphScale
tooltips.text: Size of the distortion pattern. Higher is finer and busier.

tooltips.name: _MorphSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the distortion animates. 0 freezes it as a static warp.

tooltips.name: _MorphAudio
tooltips.text: Makes the distortion react to AudioLink. The base Distortion Amount still applies in silence; audio adds on top of it.

tooltips.name: _MorphBand
tooltips.text: Which audio band drives the morph.

tooltips.name: _PlasmaViewMode
tooltips.text: Where this effect appears. Everywhere is normal. Mirrors & Cameras Only hides it on your real body but shows it in reflections and photos. Normal View Only does the reverse.

tooltips.name: _HoloViewMode
tooltips.text: Where this effect appears. Everywhere is normal. Mirrors & Cameras Only hides it on your real body but shows it in reflections and photos. Normal View Only does the reverse.

tooltips.name: _StarViewMode
tooltips.text: Where this effect appears. Everywhere is normal. Mirrors & Cameras Only hides it on your real body but shows it in reflections and photos. Normal View Only does the reverse.

tooltips.name: _MorphViewMode
tooltips.text: Where this effect appears. Everywhere is normal. Mirrors & Cameras Only hides it on your real body but shows it in reflections and photos. Normal View Only does the reverse.

tooltips.name: _EQEnable
tooltips.text: Draws a live audio equaliser across the surface, with bars that rise and fall to the music.

tooltips.name: _StarEnable
tooltips.text: Turns the surface into a window onto a starfield, with drifting stars, constellation lines, and an optional nebula.

tooltips.name: _MorphFlowMap
tooltips.text: Your own distortion map, used by the Texture pattern. The red channel pushes horizontally and green vertically, with mid grey meaning no push, the same convention as a flow map. Paint your own motion here.

tooltips.name: _MorphTiling
tooltips.text: Extra tiling and offset for the distortion pattern. X and Y stretch it independently, so you can make wide bands or tall streaks rather than square ripples; Z and W shift it.

tooltips.name: _MorphMask
tooltips.text: Optional mask limiting where the morph applies. White distorts, black stays still, so you can swim the clothing and leave the face alone. Sampled undistorted, so the mask itself never drifts.

tooltips.name: _MorphMaskInvert
tooltips.text: Flips the mask, so black areas distort instead of white.

tooltips.name: _MorphALBoost
tooltips.text: How much the audio deepens the distortion on top of the base amount. 0 means audio has no effect on depth.

tooltips.name: _MorphALSpeed
tooltips.text: How much the audio speeds up the warp. 0 keeps a steady speed and only the depth reacts.

tooltips.name: _MorphMultBand
tooltips.text: A second band that scales the primary signal, so one frequency can gate another.

tooltips.name: _MorphMultAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly the multiplier band scales the signal. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _MorphAddBand
tooltips.text: A band added on top of the primary signal, for a second frequency to contribute directly.

tooltips.name: _MorphAddAmt
tooltips.text: How much the additive band contributes. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _MorphVolBoost
tooltips.text: Scales the reaction by the overall volume across all bands, so quiet passages react less.

tooltips.name: _MorphVolAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly overall volume boosts the reaction.

tooltips.name: _StarALEnable
tooltips.text: Turns AudioLink reactivity on for the constellation. Off gives a still starfield that ignores music entirely.

tooltips.name: _StarMultBand
tooltips.text: A second band that scales the primary signal, so one frequency can gate another.

tooltips.name: _StarMultAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly the multiplier band scales the signal. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _StarAddBand
tooltips.text: A band added on top of the primary signal.

tooltips.name: _StarAddAmt
tooltips.text: How much the additive band contributes. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _StarVolBoost
tooltips.text: Scales the reaction by overall volume across all bands, so quiet passages react less.

tooltips.name: _StarVolAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly overall volume boosts the reaction.

tooltips.name: _RoomVariety
tooltips.text: How much each window's room differs. Rotates and mirrors the interior per window so one cubemap reads as many different rooms. 0 makes every window identical.

tooltips.name: _RoomVaryTint
tooltips.text: How much the colour temperature varies between windows, so some rooms read warmer or cooler than others.

tooltips.name: _RoomVaryDepth
tooltips.text: How much room depth varies between windows, so they are not all the same size box.

tooltips.name: _RoomFurnTex
tooltips.text: Cut-out furniture or silhouettes drawn inside the room. Alpha decides what is solid, so transparent areas show the back wall behind. Leave empty for an empty room.

tooltips.name: _RoomFurnDepth
tooltips.text: How far into the room the furniture sits. Low is right against the glass, high is near the back wall. Mid values give the strongest parallax.

tooltips.name: _RoomFurnScale
tooltips.text: Size of the furniture within the room.

tooltips.name: _RoomFurnVariety
tooltips.text: Shifts which part of the furniture texture each window uses, so windows show different contents. Lay the texture out as a grid of items to get the most from this.

tooltips.name: _RoomLightEnable
tooltips.text: Lights the interiors, with each window independently on or off.

tooltips.name: _RoomLitChance
tooltips.text: What fraction of windows are lit at any time. 0 is a dark building, 1 lights them all.

tooltips.name: _RoomLightColor
tooltips.text: Colour of the interior lighting. Warm yellows read as domestic, cold whites as offices.

tooltips.name: _RoomLightStrength
tooltips.text: How brightly lit rooms glow.

tooltips.name: _RoomFlicker
tooltips.text: Adds an unsteady flicker to lit windows, like a television or a failing bulb.

tooltips.name: _RoomSwitching
tooltips.text: How often windows switch between lit and dark. 0 keeps them fixed.

tooltips.name: _RoomGlassType
tooltips.text: What kind of glass this is. Static Imperfection is fixed distortion baked into the pane, like real window glass: it never animates, and the view through it shifts only as you move. Ripple animates continuously, for water, aquariums, and heat haze.

tooltips.name: _RoomGlassScale
tooltips.text: Size of the imperfections in the pane. Low is broad gentle waviness, high is fine rippled texture.

tooltips.name: _RoomGlassStreak
tooltips.text: Stretches the imperfections vertically, like the draw marks in old rolled or antique glass. 0 keeps them evenly blobby.

tooltips.name: _RoomGlassSpeed
tooltips.text: How fast the ripple moves, for the animated glass type.

tooltips.name: _IridMode
tooltips.text: Gradient blends between three colours you pick, for full artistic control. Thin Film simulates real interference in a microscopically thin coating, so the colours and their angular sweep are physically derived rather than chosen.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmNm
tooltips.text: Thickness of the film in nanometres. This is the single control that decides which colours appear: thin films give broad pale sweeps, thicker ones give tighter repeating rainbows. Soap bubbles sit around 300 to 600.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmIOR
tooltips.text: Refractive index of the film. Higher bends light more inside the coating and shifts the whole palette. Soap and oil are around 1.3 to 1.5.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmVary
tooltips.text: How much the film thickness drifts across the surface, so the colours swirl like a real film pooling and thinning instead of sitting at one flat hue.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmScale
tooltips.text: Size of the thickness variation pattern. Low is broad lazy swirls, high is fine marbling.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmSat
tooltips.text: How saturated the interference colours are. 1 is the physical result; lower desaturates toward a pearly sheen, higher exaggerates it.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmFresnel
tooltips.text: Concentrates the effect toward grazing angles, where light travels furthest through the film and interference is strongest in reality. 0 applies it evenly across the surface.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmTintAmt
tooltips.text: How much the interference colours the base surface as well as its highlights. Low keeps it to a sheen on top; high stains the material itself.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmSpace
tooltips.text: Which space the thickness variation is sampled in. Object Space flows continuously over the whole mesh, so the film has no seams where UV islands meet, and it moves with the avatar. UV0 follows the texture layout instead, which is useful if you want the swirl to line up with painted detail, but it will show hard edges at UV seams.

tooltips.name: _IridALEnable
tooltips.text: Turns AudioLink reactivity on for the iridescence. Off keeps the colours steady and ignores music entirely.

tooltips.name: _IridMultBand
tooltips.text: A second band that scales the primary signal, so one frequency can gate another.

tooltips.name: _IridMultAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly the multiplier band scales the signal. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _IridAddBand
tooltips.text: A band added on top of the primary signal.

tooltips.name: _IridAddAmt
tooltips.text: How much the additive band contributes. 0 disables it.

tooltips.name: _IridVolBoost
tooltips.text: Scales the reaction by overall volume across all bands, so quiet passages react less.

tooltips.name: _IridVolAmt
tooltips.text: How strongly overall volume boosts the reaction.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmRamp
tooltips.text: Optional colour palette, read left to right. The interference still decides which parts of the surface shift and how they sweep with viewing angle; the ramp only decides which colours those bands are. Use it to get a gold and teal oil slick, or a pink and green pearl, instead of the natural spectrum.

tooltips.name: _IridFilmRampAmt
tooltips.text: How far the natural interference colours are replaced by the palette ramp. 0 keeps the physically derived spectrum, 1 uses the ramp entirely.

tooltips.name: _RefractMode
tooltips.text: Screen Offset pushes the background sideways by the surface angle, which is cheap and easy to art direct. Physical IOR bends the view ray by Snell's law using a real index of refraction, giving correct dispersion, thickness response and roughness scattering.

tooltips.name: _RefractIOR
tooltips.text: How strongly the glass bends light. Water is about 1.33, window glass 1.5, sapphire 1.77, diamond 2.42. Higher values distort the background more and push the prism fringes further apart.

tooltips.name: _RefractThickness
tooltips.text: How much glass the light travels through. Thicker glass shifts the background further and absorbs more of the tint colour.

tooltips.name: _RefractDispersion
tooltips.text: How differently each colour bends. This is what splits white light into a rainbow at the edges, as in a prism. Real crown glass is subtle; large values give an exaggerated jewel look.

tooltips.name: _RefractRough
tooltips.text: Frosts the glass, scattering what shows through instead of transmitting it sharply.

tooltips.name: _RefractSamples
tooltips.text: How many taps the roughness blur uses. Higher is smoother but costs more; only raise it if you can see banding in frosted glass.

tooltips.name: _RefractFresnel
tooltips.text: Fades refraction toward grazing angles, where real glass reflects rather than transmits, letting the surface's own shading take over at the silhouette.

tooltips.name: _RefractAbsorb
tooltips.text: Colour the glass absorbs as light passes through it, applied more strongly the thicker the glass. This is how coloured glass gets deeper in tone at its thickest points.
